proposals.title: Monorepo bootstrap with npm workspaces, strict TypeScript, and blocking lint gates
proposals.why_now: TASK-0001 has been rejected twice. The root cause in both reviews is that pnpm is not available as a standard executable in the authoritative validation environment — it resolves to /workspace/pnpm rather than a PATH-accessible binary. The spec does not mandate pnpm; npm workspaces provide the same monorepo capability and npm is reliably available in all Node.js environments. Switching package manager is the minimal change that removes the environmental blocker. The secondary REVIEW-002 finding (TypeScript compilation silently excluding .tsx, .mts, .cts files) must also be fixed. Nothing else in FASE-1 can start without the directory structure, strict TypeScript configuration, and blocking lint gates in place.

proposals.title: Write the three DEFINIR ADRs required before packages/core can be implemented
proposals.why_now: ADR-009 is an explicit FASE-1 acceptance criterion: the CanonicalEncoder must be specified in its own ADR before any state hash exists. ADR-002 requires the hash function to be specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before any rand() implementation. ADR-004 marks the technical enforcement mechanism for rounding-mode declaration as DEFINIR. All three must be resolved and recorded before packages/core work begins; implementing core before these ADRs embeds unrecorded decisions that cannot be reversed without breaking encodingVersion and invalidating all frozen StateHash references.

proposals.title: packages/core — branded numeric types, positional RNG, CanonicalEncoder, and arithmetic helpers
proposals.why_now: packages/core is the dependency of every other pure package. Without branded types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick), the type system cannot enforce ADR-003 or ADR-004 and violations accumulate silently from the first domain file. Without the positional rand(), packages/world cannot be written. Without CanonicalEncoder, no StateHash can be computed and INV-01, INV-17, INV-22 have no foundation. This package must exist before any other domain code; the ADRs from IDEA-002 must precede it to avoid embedding unrecorded decisions.

proposals.title: packages/world price generator, packages/domain ledger and spot orders, packages/application canonical tick loop
proposals.why_now: These three packages compose the functional core of FASE-1 and must arrive together: application is the only layer that composes world and domain without coupling them (§14.5). The price generator is the entry point for INV-02, which the spec identifies as the most important test in the project. The double-entry ledger is the entry point for INV-04 through INV-07. The canonical tick loop implements the ten-step locked order from §7 — an explicit FASE-1 acceptance criterion. None of the FASE-1 invariants INV-01 through INV-07 can be verified without all three packages.

proposals.title: tools/replay, tools/bench, minimum Electron UI, and Windows/Linux installers to complete FASE-1 acceptance
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires tools/replay (reporting first divergent tick), tools/bench (with frozen calibration ratios and p95 protocol), a minimum UI (lightweight-charts price chart, BRL balance, buy/sell buttons, pause/1x controls, permanent non-dismissable Portuguese disclaimer per §20), and an installer for Windows and Linux. The spec warns that deferred packaging leads to unrecoverable ABI failures. The performance baseline must be frozen at the end of FASE-1; there is no meaningful baseline to freeze until the simulation kernel exists.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — price generator transcendental functions: §5.1 constructs prices in log-space, requiring log and exp. Both are prohibited in pure packages by §13. An ADR specifying a fixed-point or lookup-table implementation that produces bit-identical results across platforms must be written before packages/world work begins. This ADR is separate from ADR-002 (hash) and ADR-009 (canonical encoder) and should be resolved as part of IDEA-004 planning.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — octave parameters: the number of octaves, their periods, and amplitudes for trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are DEFINIR per §5.1. These parameters must be fixed in a versioned configuration file with an ADR before the price generator is implemented, because any post-implementation change requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all reference StateHashes frozen in tools/bench.
